$comment: Single source of truth for kun engine metadata. Prose/docs reference this file instead of hardcoding numbers. /health (.claude/scripts/health.sh) reads it and warns when docs or reality drift from these values. Agent frontmatter uses a model alias (`opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku` per `model_tiers`) — never pin a version number there.
$model_comment: `model` is the Claude Code SESSION default only — set by Abdout via /model on 2026-09-26 (the `opus` alias resolves to it). `fallback_models` mirrors settings.json `fallbackModel`: current-generation, subscription-covered, never Fable. Nothing else may reuse these fields: the social Hub's draft-model chain is owned by src/components/root/social/knobs.ts + scripts/drain-drafts.sh (4f2bd76 once overwrote this field with the social default).

billing.$comment: Max 5x ($100/mo) for the time being — corrected from Max 20x on 2026-06-12. Subscription-ONLY posture: no paid usage credits, no API-key per-token spend — except the plan's included API credits for scrape vision readers ($10) and the mkan /find agent ($15), each hard-capped in code (D-20261021-included-api-credits-for-readers, D-20261021-included-api-credits-for-find) — changing this requires a /decide entry + Abdout approval (captain ESCALATE gate: budget > $50/mo). Check /usage per-category weekly to stay inside plan caps.

sync.$comment: Self-update stamps per tier — /sync refreshes them; the captain flags overdue tiers at session start. null = never synced (due immediately). Sources of the form gh:owner/repo are read via `gh api .../releases`. Material adoptions land in docs/CONFIG-BENCHMARK.md → Adoption log.

anthropic: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/<page>.md — append .md to any docs page for raw markdown (settings-reference, skills, sub-agents, hooks, memory, best-practices)
practice: community Claude Code configs — survey set in docs/CONFIG-BENCHMARK.md → Sources
https://nextjs.org/evals — per-model cost + pass rate on agentic Next.js tasks
sources.$comment: Vercel is legacy since the 2026-09 Cloudflare move — headlines only. Stack sweeps also read each vendor's own agent guidance (bundled docs, AGENTS.md, official MCP servers and skills).

counts.$plugins_comment: The two plugins are how the fleet reaches other machines. kun-company also carries the rules, pattern cards, hooks, and workflows. Union of both skill sets is 61 (build ships in both).

eval.$comment: Declared POLICY for the bench layers. Measured state lives in .claude/memory/skill-scores.json — never here, because every engine.json field is something health.sh checks reality against and a score has no declared counterpart. listing_cap is a shared, zero-sum budget: the fleet listing is loaded into EVERY session before a word is typed, so accuracy bought with prefix bloat is a regression, not a win. Raising a cap is a deliberate, recorded act — never a silent accommodation of the thing that just breached it.

listing_cap_history.why: absorbed two deliberate additions made before any baseline existed: the deploy frontmatter fix (+640, a proven dispatch defect) and the bench skill itself (+596). Trimming draft/higgs prose would also have fit under 26000, but tuning descriptions before the first measurement is exactly what this system exists to stop. The next reset requires evidence from a scored run.

20 of 67 skills had NO when_to_use at all, so they were reachable only by typing their exact name — unusable under kun's actual operating model, where Abdout never types slash commands. Writing them added ~5.5k chars. The previous cap only held because a third of the fleet was undocumented, which makes it an artifact of incompleteness rather than a budget. Note the cap was always a PROXY for the real question — does more text hurt dispatch? — and that question is now directly measurable, so the cap's remaining job is token-cost control while /bench measures quality. The re-run at fnv1a:9fd4080f tests the trade.

the fleet sat at 31,981/32,000 — nineteen characters of headroom — so the cap had stopped governing bloat and started vetoing capability: ANY new skill breached it regardless of how lean it was. The scrape skill was trimmed from 754 chars to 436 (still yielding 21 dispatch cases) BEFORE this raise was proposed, so the 500 buys back headroom rather than accommodating the thing that breached it. The alternative — trimming draft/higgs/approve/publish to make room — was rejected as unmeasured tuning of deliberate negative-discrimination clauses, which the 2026-08-06 entry warns against. Whether the added text costs dispatch accuracy is the bench's question, and the baseline is owed a reset regardless: corpus_hash has been stale since the record commit (scored=67, fleet=69).

the measured fleet stood at 32,422/32,500 — 78 characters of headroom — so the cap had returned to the exact state the 2026-08-17 entry describes: it had stopped governing bloat and started vetoing capability, because ANY new skill breaches it however lean. /funnel was written tight from the start rather than trimmed after the fact: 390 chars against /scrape's 436, and /scrape is the lane it mirrors — so the 500 buys back headroom rather than accommodating the thing that breached it, which is the test the 2026-08-06 entry sets. The alternative was trimming the next tier down (auth 816, feature 726, deploy 713, qa 685); rejected because none has been scored and 'tuning descriptions before the first measurement is exactly what this system exists to stop'. The four heaviest (draft/higgs/approve/publish, 3,862 together) carry deliberate negative-discrimination clauses and stay untouched. Leaves 188 chars of headroom, so the next addition faces the same deliberate decision rather than a silent one. NOTE: this raise is Abdout's call to keep or revert — it is recorded here so the state is coherent and health.sh passes, not to settle the question by default.

the fleet stood at 32,999/33,000 — one character of headroom — so ANY new skill breached it however lean, the state the 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18 entries describe. /reverse (REA feature teardown) was written tight from the start: trimmed from ~680 to 251 chars (5 dispatch cases) BEFORE this raise, against /funnel's 390. Trimming higgs/deploy/report/draft/pwa prose to fit was tried and reverted: those are unscored negative-discrimination clauses, which every earlier entry leaves untouched. Measured after: 33,250, leaving 250 chars of headroom so the next addition faces the same deliberate decision. NOTE: Abdout's call to keep or revert, recorded so the state is coherent and health.sh passes.

eval.$harness_listing_comment: The HARNESS budget (settings.json skillListingBudgetFraction), not listing_cap: Claude Code drops the descriptions of the least-used skills once the listing passes this share of the context window. Raised 0.01 → 0.02 by Abdout on 2026-09-26 after /skill-doctor showed ~110 skills listed name-only. listing_cap (kun's own fleet chars) is unchanged and still governs bloat.

model_tiers.$comment: Per-agent model alias by task type. The portable stack fleet (~/.claude/agents) follows this; the project fleet defaults to opus (quality-over-speed) except purely mechanical agents. Every agent also carries `effort:` frontmatter per delegation.efforts (added 2026-07-26). Aliases resolve forward on their own (opus → Opus 5.5 since 2.1.280; sonnet → Sonnet 5.5 since 2.1.284; haiku → Haiku 5.5 since 2.1.293).
model_tiers.fable: escalation only — switch the main loop to Fable 5.1 with /model when Opus 5.5 at xhigh falls short on long-horizon work. Never in agent frontmatter, fallbacks, or headless `claude -p` / Agent SDK runs: there Fable can bill usage credits with no consent prompt (code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config).
model_tiers.opus: the main loop (session default Opus 5.5 since 2026-09-26) + architecture, orchestration, deep reasoning, code review/fixes, and strategy/leadership agents (incl. captain)
model_tiers.sonnet: standard build agents + the mechanical project agent (package)
model_tiers.haiku: routine/formatting agents (comment, git, icon, github, semantic, sse, structure)

delegation.$comment: Token-economy routing — three axes: model tier × effort × product lane. Playbook: docs/TOKEN-ECONOMY.md; on-demand audit: /economy. Facts that shape it (re-verified 2026-09-26): models from Opus 4.7 on use a larger tokenizer (~35% more tokens than pre-4.7 for the same text); Opus 5.5 and Fable cannot turn thinking off — effort is the lever; prompt-cache TTL is 1h on subscription; Opus 5.5 lists at 2x Sonnet 5 per token ($4/$20 vs $2/$10 — it was ~5x in the Opus 4.x era), and on nextjs.org/evals it solved more for less per task (UNVERIFIED whether plan-window burn tracks list price).

efforts.low: haiku agents — mechanical/formatting work (comment, git, icon, github, semantic, sse, structure); workflow stages that transform rather than reason. The `haiku` alias resolves to Haiku 5.5 (Claude Code 2.1.293+), which takes effort, so `effort: low` now applies on haiku agents (was a no-op on Haiku 4.5).
efforts.medium: sonnet build agents — standard implementation with known patterns
efforts.high: opus specialists — default ceiling for agents; review, fixes, product references, strategy
efforts.xhigh: judgment tier ONLY — captain, architecture, orchestration; main-loop deep design on explicit request
efforts.policy: every agent carries `effort:` frontmatter matching its model tier; Workflow scripts pass opts.effort per stage (low for mechanical stages, high+ only for verify/judge)

products.$comment: All Anthropic surfaces draw the SAME Max pool (5h session window + weekly window, shared with chat and Cowork). Product delegation optimizes tokens-per-outcome, not separate quotas — only the a/h lanes are off-pool.
products.claude-code: build work only — heaviest per-turn context (rules + MCP + repo files travel with every message)
products.cowork: planning, research, decisions, docs — no repo/MCP preamble; handoff via ~/.claude/bridge.md
products.claude-chat: pure Q&A, drafting, brainstorming — cheapest surface, zero engine preamble; use before opening a Code session for think-work
products.claude-web-code: long-running cloud babysitting (autofix-pr, scheduled routines) — same pool, so keep routines lean and infrequent
products.antigravity: OFF-POOL cheap lane (`a` = Gemini) — easy one-file mechanical tasks; zero Anthropic tokens
products.hermes: OFF-POOL chat relay (`h` = free Nous model) — gateway/channel tasks, never build work itself; it hands build work to Claude Code through scripts/hermes/claude.sh (ON-POOL: Opus 5.5 on the Max plan, Abdout only, one at a time, 15 runs/day)

lanes.$comment: The dispatch table (2026-11-01): which lane, model and effort a kind of work goes to. Read by the main session (.claude/CLAUDE.md → Dispatch) and explained in content/docs/interconnection.mdx. Workflow stages must name model + effort (lint-contracts → workflow-effort).
lanes.mechanical: haiku agents (git, comment, icon, github, semantic, sse, structure) — low effort
lanes.judge: opus specialists or Workflow verify stages — high effort
lanes.fan_out: a Workflow (qa, handover, textbook, scrape, …) — per-stage model + effort
lanes.long_or_recurring: a loop through .claude/bin/kun-claude.sh — ledgered, lean when it needs no skills or MCP
lanes.off_pool: Antigravity (`a`, Gemini) — easy one-file tasks, zero Anthropic tokens
lanes.other_session: ListAgents → SendMessage (Code ↔ Code, any of Abdout's machines)

delegation.session_hygiene: /clear between unrelated tasks (stale context taxes every message); /compact with focus instructions on long tasks; batch touches inside the 1h cache window — a >1h idle gap reprocesses full context; plan mode before big builds; specific prompts over broad scans

devices.$comment: Declared POLICY for the Mac ↔ iPhone ↔ Claude-surface lane, read by .claude/scripts/devices.sh (--status, --brief at SessionStart, --install). Measured state is never stored here — devices.sh reads it live. Facts verified against code.claude.com docs on 2026-09-27 (remote-control, mobile, desktop, settings-reference, env-vars): push is two settings keys (agentPushNotifEnabled, inputNeededNotifEnabled, both default false); `max` effort cannot be saved as a default (session-only unless CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL pins it, which also overrides every agent's effort frontmatter — never set it); Dispatch is closed to new users; the Claude app offers Manual / Accept edits / Plan for Remote Control sessions, so the server's starting mode is set here.

rc_server.$comment: One `claude remote-control` server in tmux, rooted at ~/kun, so the Claude app's Code tab can start sessions on the Mac without a terminal left open for it. same-dir, never worktree (main-only rule). Capacity is sized to 16 GB of RAM: each session carries its own MCP processes.
rc_server.name: Mac · kun

presence.$comment: The marker CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE points at (settings.json env). Present = input within idle_seconds and the screen unlocked; pushes are held while it exists.

warn.$comment: SessionStart --brief thresholds. The 2026-09-27 audit found 3 GB free, 19 GB swapped and 9 sessions open; builds hit ENOSPC near 98% (2026-09-22).

hygiene.$comment: Read by maintain.sh / maintain.ps1 step_disk (approved by Abdout 2026-09-27): when the daily heartbeat finds less than prune_below_gb free, it prunes only self-rebuilding caches — uv, the pnpm store, Docker build cache above docker_cache_cap_gb, Docker images older than docker_image_age that no container uses, then TRIMs the colima disk so the Mac gets the space back. Never repos, .next folders, or anything a running container needs.
hygiene.$container_comment: Approved by Abdout 2026-11-03 (e3517cf7): containers stopped longer than docker_container_idle_days are removed, except one holding an anonymous volume (it would be orphaned). Named volumes and bind mounts keep their data, and volumes are never pruned. Docker is left alone while a deploy build runs.
hygiene.$cf_build_comment: Approved by Abdout 2026-11-01: ~/.cache/cf-build/<repo> folders with no file newer than this many days are removed (each deploy wipes and rebuilds its own folder anyway). Folders only — files and anything named *env* (production dotenvs) are never touched.

notify.$comment: Team channels for .claude/scripts/lib/notify.sh / scripts/lib/notify.mjs (kun_notify <channel> <subject> <text>). `me` is NOT here: it is per machine (~/.claude/.kun-notify), so a teammate's alerts never land in Abdout's DM. Transport: hermes send → desktop banner → stderr.

improve.$comment: Declared POLICY for the LEARN layer (.claude/scripts/improve.mjs → /sync tier `self`, 2026-11-01). Detection is zero tokens and runs daily in the heartbeat; findings live in ~/.claude/state/findings.json. SAFE local fixes apply automatically; SAFE repo fixes are applied and committed by /sync self; DECIDE rows wait in ONE rolling issue (label engine-decision) for Abdout's `yes <id>`. Only the owner Mac (the one running aware's launchd refresher) writes that issue.

resolver.$comment: Declared POLICY for .claude/scripts/resolve.mjs (the UserPromptSubmit router, 2026-11-01). global_blocks: hogwarts blocks distinctive enough to hint from ANY session (curated by Abdout's choice: curated list, one-line hint) — generic ones (docs, table, finance, grades, listings, dashboard, settings) stay local. never_bare: repo names too common in prose to route without an explicit form.

aware.$comment: Declared POLICY for the SENSE layer (.claude/scripts/aware.mjs, 2026-11-01). Measured state lives in ~/.claude/state/aware.json, never here. Alerts fire on transitions only (two refreshes in a row), once each, at most alert_cap_per_day; spend, sync, bench and dirty files are shown, never alerted.

jobs.$comment: Declared POLICY for every scheduled job. runs.sh judges (each job's own record in ~/.claude/state/runs/<job>.json first, then launchd, log mtimes and ~/.claude/logs/runs.jsonl); supervise.mjs acts on that judgment (re-fire, heal, escalate). Measured state never lives here; schedules stay in the plists and Hermes jobs.json, never copied. cadence_hours 0 = a KeepAlive daemon; kind trigger = a WatchPaths job. owner → $owners (where its issue and Slack line go). resume: auto (re-fire a missed or failed slot, up to max_attempts started runs) · tick (one early run on wake, never per slot) · alert (never re-fire) · heal (restart when down). needs: what the gate waits for besides a full wake and the network (twenty, vault, docker, neon, github, slack). max_wait: minutes job-run.sh waits for the gate before recording defer. max_minutes: the run cap. deadline_hours: an ok is due this long after a slot, or the watchdog outside the Mac alerts. refire: the entry point that re-runs this job's slot. only_if undelivered: re-fire only when Hermes ran it but the Slack send failed. mac_only false marks a job that needs nothing on the Mac.
jobs.$notify: per machine — ~/.claude/.kun-notify holds this machine's `me` target (e.g. slack:<DM id>); never fleet config, or every teammate's digest lands in one person's DM
jobs.$lean_comment: Headless claude runs whose job name starts with one of these prefixes run lean through .claude/bin/kun-claude.sh: no MCP servers, no skill listing (-43% tokens per run, measured 2026-11-01). Only for jobs that use neither skills/Workflow nor MCP tools; drain-drafts (/draft skill), textbook (Workflow) and hermes (full sessions) stay full.

hermes:mkan-sprint-runner.$comment: mkan /monetize sprint prompts in full auto (mkan scripts/crm/hermes/sprint-runner.sh): one headless Claude Code run per tick, MKAN_UNATTENDED=1 so nothing reaches a real person; the cap is read by kun-claude.sh (KUN_JOB = this name)

$cloud.$comment: Schedules that run off the Mac, checked by supervise.mjs every check_minutes. gh: the newest scheduled run per workflow (failed: its failed jobs re-run once, live for live_owners; disabled for inactivity: enabled again; no run for 2x its period + 2 h: stale). workers: each cron route's newest run in Workers Logs, via the telemetry API (Keychain cloudflare-api); status 500+ red, no run for 2x its period + 15 min stale; alert only. The cron maps are each repo's cf/crons.json. Not listed: kun domains.yml (the local domains job runs the same probe and alerts its blocking items itself) and codebase claude-specialized-tasks.yml (dormant, disabled by GitHub for inactivity; it would spend API credits).

$supervise.$comment: live, heal and alerts are on for every owner (mkan first, kun and hogwarts since 2026-11-02 evening). Set live false and list owners in live_owners to stage a rollout again; the rest then log would-fire. supervise.mjs writes every decision to ~/.claude/state/supervise.json.

textbook.$comment: Declared POLICY for the textbook pipeline (PDF -> verified Markdown twin). Measured state lives in .claude/memory/textbook-scores.json - never here. Thresholds remain PROVISIONAL but are now backed by FIVE graded books (biology .948 B, math .967 A, physics .953 A, chemistry .946 B, math-specialized .936 B) rather than one. Two structural facts drive the 2026-09-29 revision: (1) a formatter hook on Write corrupts pages identically in BOTH reads, so no agreement score in this pipeline can detect it - the Preflight canary is the only defence and the run now ABORTS when it fails; (2) render kind and reference direction are PER-BOOK facts - 16 of 25 sd/g12 pdfs are vector (1000px throws away detail) and reference order tracks the digit script (Latin EN books store reversed, Arabic-Indic AN books store as drawn), so carrying one book's answer to the next reverses every reference in it.

thresholds.set_on: 5 books (biology, math, physics, chemistry, math-specialized), opus, 2026-09-09..29

textbook.headline: random-sample seq agreement only — the risk tail and post-adjudication scores are reported beside it, never folded in

models.$comment: 2026-10-10, biology corpus (30 pages, 499 assertions, contract sha1:d6a20313b1cc, both runs audited CLEAN): blind sonnet-v1 0.9639 vs blind opus-v1 0.9379. Sonnet won numerals (226/226 vs 209/226) and RTL tables (172/178 vs 157/178); opus won only figure labels (12/15 vs 9/15). Both earlier 'baselines' (0.9621, 0.9741) were SHIPPED twins — opus transcription + adjudication — not blind reads, so they were never the right yardstick. The blind audit read stays opus: a second read by a different model does not share the first one's blind spots.

preflight.formatter_canary: MANDATORY. An agent writes 5) / 9) / '- +' through the Write TOOL and reads the bytes back; a shell write does not fire PostToolUse hooks and proves nothing. Failure ABORTS the run - a corrupted page is invisible to every downstream score.
preflight.classifies: vector vs scan from TEXT-LAYER presence (not image count: chemistry averages 0.2 images/page yet carries a 1575px figure); vector -> re-render the page at 3x for small glyphs instead of marking them illegible
preflight.reference_direction: measured from the text layer by comparing a stored digit-run against its drawn x-order; needs >= 8 runs or it honestly returns unknown (2 runs once produced a confident verdict that a 3x render contradicted)
preflight.crop_native_caveat: textbook-crop.py native inspects EMBEDDED RASTERS ONLY - zoomHelps:false does NOT mean 'cannot be read better' on a vector page

textbook.render_note: shipped pages/*.webp stay 1000px (the reader serves them); hi-res renders are for transcription only and are never shipped
textbook.batch_note: 12 measured a higher stall rate under the 600s no-progress watchdog; 8 keeps an agent's lifetime under it. Pages are written one at a time and survive a kill, so a stall costs time, not work.
textbook.concurrency_note: the ~8-agent cap is PER WORKFLOW, not global; 4 concurrent books exhausted a usage window in 13 minutes and left 4 half-books. One book at a time, to completion.
textbook.cost_note: verify+adjudicate costs MORE than transcription on a small book (math: 3.49M verify vs ~1.8M transcribe). Enriching the contract is the only lever that has paid: it cut physics' queued pages 24 -> 10 and verify 3.49M -> 2.15M.

coverage.$comment: 2026-10-24 (Abdout: '100% accurate to the latest PDF'). sample = only the headline sample + risk tail are re-read, so ~85% of a book's pages are never measured. full = EVERY page gets an independent witness and every non-clean page (ordering included) is adjudicated; the twin front matter carries coverage / verifiedPages / unsettled. The headline stays the random sample's seq so grades remain comparable across modes.
witness_order: textlayer (md-agreement.py --witness textlayer) — free; clears only skeleton >= 0.98 pages with <= 2 numerals, no table, no figure labels
blind model read (auditModel) — every page the free witnesses cannot clear, and ALWAYS the random sample
coverage.textlayer_measured: 21 landed g12 twins: the layer is usable on 5 (art .99 / home-economics .95 health; biology .48, engineering .32, agriculture .15) and absent or mojibake on 16. Strict clearance 0-20 pages per book (~5-10% where usable). Its value is the OMISSION detector: pages whose PDF text holds >15% more words than the twin are force-queued even when both model reads agree; after furniture + alt-text handling it flagged no real omission in the 5 usable landed books. Skeleton cannot see numerals (gold p39 biology: skeleton .987 hid a numeric error) — numerals never clear.

routing.$comment: Who does what, cheapest first; a swap is adopted only when a blind textbook-bench run on the corpus scores >= the current model AND the text-layer/gold false-clean rate is 0. Status 'adopted' = in use; 'bench' = wired but not yet adopted.

transcribe.bench: haiku REJECTED 2026-10-25 (haiku-v1, audit CLEAN): 0.952 vs sonnet 0.964 on the g12 biology corpus — weak on table direction 0.63, labels 0.73, illegible 0.80; stronger on latin 0.99 vs 0.94, numerals 1.0. Re-bench only on a latin-book corpus

witness.bench: Gemini 3.8 Flash via agy -p (off the Claude pool; blocked 2026-10-24: Google account 'not eligible for Antigravity' until verified in a browser) · haiku (different model, cheaper; its misses cost adjudications, not false agreement)

routing.free_tools: PyMuPDF triage + text-layer skeleton witness, md-structure grid lint, md-table-direction crops, pdftoppm/imagehash for edition matching (catalog verify sources). tesseract measured weak on these scans (2026-09-09) — not a witness.

textbook.exit_gate: a run is reportable only when agents_error == 0 AND the book appears in textbook-scores.json. A window death during Adjudicate still returns degraded:false, repaired:0 and a letter grade - that is NOT a finished book. Recovery is mode:repair, which reuses the surviving queue.json.

loop.$comment: The nightly textbook loop (scripts/textbook/loop.sh, launchd com.databayt.textbook-loop). Each tick: sense (catalog `pnpm twins --cdn`) -> pick (in-progress book first, then priority) -> stage into catalog/.work -> claude -p runs the textbook workflow capped at pages_per_tick NEW pages (resumable; a complete book is verified + adjudicated + persisted in the same call) -> scripts/textbook/land.sh publishes when the twin gate passes -> one comment on the tracking issue. Sundays: textbook-contract.py --promote -> presets proposals.
loop.grades_note: g12 -> g1 (Abdout, 2026-10-24). A book whose catalog book gate fails (no verification block: all of g1-g11 today) is skipped by pick() until `pnpm verify` records its edition — so listing a grade arms it, verifying it opens it.
loop.ticks_note: two starts inside the window (Abdout, 2026-10-24: subscription only, more ticks). Add a third only when /usage shows weekly room — a full-coverage book costs ~2x a sampled one.
loop.priority_note: worst text first: OCR twins (scans, fonts without a Unicode map) before text-layer twins; fewer pages first within a kind so books finish and publish sooner
loop.pages_note: ~120 pages x 9k tokens ~= 1.1M tokens of transcription per night; a ~180-page book finishes in two nights and verifies (+~2M) on the second
loop.sample_note: 24, not 12, for loop books: two random 12-page samples of the SAME chemistry twin scored 0.946 and 0.893 (2026-10-09). 12 more blind re-reads cost ~110k tokens per book and halve that swing.
loop.model_note: transcribe/audit/adjudicate follow textbook.models — decided by the 2026-10-10 blind bench pair
loop.publish_rule: the catalog twin gate passes on the new twin (vision, agreement >= thresholds.B, agreementSample >= 12, every page transcribed, sourceMd5) — NOT 'new >= live': random samples of one twin differ by ~5 points

presets.$comment: Cross-book contract clauses by subject kind, in the textbook skill's scripts/presets.json. textbook-contract.py appends the matching kinds to every NEW contract (--preset to force one). A clause is promoted only with evidence from >= 2 books; seed clauses for kinds with no transcribed book yet are marked seed. The loop's Sunday step proposes new ones (--promote).

media.$comment: Budgets for every still and video the media library ships (edit/scripts/media.sh: encode, derive, qa-pack; read by media-qa). Free + local by decision (2026-10-07): no paid generation API. Sizes in MB unless noted.
